lines: I marked where the raiders came through. I also marked where you turned them back.
Maps make borders look calm. You reminded me borders have to be defended.
I can point to where you met them. That spot feels different now.
A village border is not ink. Yesterday, you made that clear.
You changed the shape of the danger before it reached the center.
I marked the raid path. I also marked where it stopped.
The map of this place has one more reason to keep its name.
You made the distance between <red><bold>raiders</bold></red> and homes matter.
When danger came close, nobody had time to sound brave first.
You learn a lot about a village when everyone hears the bell at once.
